selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What central truth is presented in this passage about the One who runs the universe?
questions.answer: The passage teaches that the One who creates, manages, and sustains the whole universe is one and has no equal, partner, helper, or rival.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the universe: as random, fragmented, or coordinated?
questions.answer: It portrays the universe as coordinated.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention substances and living or purposeful beings together?
questions.answer: To show that both the materials of the world and the beings active within it fit into one common system.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that the same kinds of elements and species are found across the earth?
questions.answer: To show that one rule and one management are operating everywhere, which points to one Lord.

questions.question: How does the image of a magnificent city support the passage’s message?
questions.answer: A great city working in harmony suggests one governing authority over all its affairs.

questions.question: Why is the earth-wide presence of the same elements and species important?
questions.answer: It shows one pattern of creation and management extending everywhere.

questions.question: What does the passage teach by saying He has neither inability nor deficiency?
questions.answer: It teaches that His power and perfection are complete, so nothing limits Him and nothing is lacking in Him.

questions.question: What does the phrase about having no partner or opposite add to the meaning?
questions.answer: It strengthens the teaching that nothing shares His rule and nothing stands against Him as an equal force.

questions.question: What moral or spiritual danger is connected to the idea of partners in this passage?
questions.answer: The passage connects it with division and corruption of the truth of divine unity.

questions.question: What is the main claim made in the Fifth Truth?
questions.answer: The main claim is that the unity and order seen throughout the whole cosmos prove that its Maker and Governor is one.

questions.question: Which parts of creation are included in this proof?
questions.answer: The proof includes the whole cosmos, its major supports, its smaller parts, and all the beings within it.

questions.question: Why does the passage focus on the whole cosmos as well as its individual parts?
questions.answer: Because unity appears both in the large picture and in the smaller details, strengthening the proof.

questions.question: How does the passage deal with the fact that many things are interwoven and similar?
questions.answer: It says that even within that overlap and similarity, one Name and one type of act appear everywhere, which supports unity.

questions.question: What kind of being is described by the terms monarch, nurturer, master, and builder?
questions.answer: They describe a being with complete authority, care, ownership, and creative control.

questions.question: What does the passage affirm about the One who made and arranges the universe?
questions.answer: It affirms that He alone rules it and that no one resembles or assists Him in that rule.

questions.question: What is the significance of saying He has no equal or peer?
questions.answer: It means no other being resembles Him in His authority, power, or right to rule.

questions.question: How does the passage view the idea of assigning partners to Allah?
questions.answer: It treats that idea as incompatible with the order and unity plainly seen in creation.

questions.question: Why is disagreement mentioned near the end?
questions.answer: To explain that multiple independent rulers would produce conflict, which does not match the harmony of the universe.

questions.question: What does the passage say exists throughout the whole universe, its supports, its parts, and its beings?
questions.answer: It says there is extremely fine order and regularity throughout all of them.

questions.question: How are the pillars and parts of the cosmos treated in relation to that order?
questions.answer: They are treated as sharing in that same order and being woven into one overall structure.

questions.question: What point is made about the Divine Names and actions working in the world?
questions.answer: They extend across everything or nearly everything, even though things are layered together and often similar in nature.

questions.question: What does the repeated emphasis on “the same” help communicate?
questions.answer: It highlights consistency and unity across different places and levels of creation.

questions.question: What tension does the passage highlight between multiplicity and unity?
questions.answer: It notes that although things are many and layered, the governing marks and actions remain unified.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying the Maker has no minister or aide?
questions.answer: It means He does not depend on assistants to carry out His will.
